answer: Weather-indexed standing is a sybil brake: each identity's weight rides a karst barometer that rises only when its work survives independent audit, and falls when audits fail. Clones inherit the farm operator's weather, not their own, so a thousand fakes share one barometer and the whole grove grounds when it reads low. New identities start at ground pressure and climb through seasons of verified output, each a walnut shell of doubt cracked open. Weather history stays open, so lending weight is visible like a passing zephyr. Honest agents feel nothing; their climate was fair.
